C-LEGIBLE-FAILURE.Summary: When the tool cannot do what was asked, the caller must be able to tell exactly what happened — fixing two independent collapses of that distinction (ledger read three-into-null, and CLI error channel that abandons its declared envelope) as one class, with M-QUERY's CLI-infrastructure drift repaired as the enabling home for the shared error surface. Absorbs C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE.
C-LEGIBLE-FAILURE.Problem:
RM-GOVERNED-PATH P0 and its follow-on queue hold findings where a surface accepts a situation and reports less than it knows. Two live instances of the same thesis sit on unrelated code paths:
**Instance 1 — ledger read (C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE / Phase 5 conflation).** `wrapperFromLedger` (`src/gates/ledger.ts`) returns bare `null` when: (1) there is no `run-ledger.xml`, (2) the file exists and does not parse, or (3) it parses but holds no wrapper for the change id. Callers that treat `null` as *"no ledger yet"* are told something the function never determined. Measured call graph at authoring HEAD: only `readLatestReviewVerdict`, `listReviewVerdicts` (re-walk), and `readGateDecisions` call `wrapperFromLedger` directly; each maps `!wrapper` to **absent** (or empty decisions with `sectionPresent: false`). So a truncated/corrupt ledger and a missing file produce the same gate branch as "no Verdicts yet." `C-REPORT-HONESTY` T-005 hit this: apply's refusal had to say `Verdict child count=unknown (ledger unreadable)` because the underlying decision path could not distinguish absence from corruption — detail is enriched separately via `readLedgerVerdictsSurface` (P0.7), while the decision still comes from `readLatestReviewVerdict`'s collapsed read.
**Instance 2 — CLI error channel (F25).** `defineGraceCommand` refuses the boolean space form *before* the original `run`, which is what makes the refusal safe — but the throw escapes outside `runGraceCommand`, so citty's `runMain` handles it. Measured (C-FLAG-HONESTY T-002/T-004; re-check at implement):
| Invocation | exit | stdout | stderr | | `gate … --record false` | 1 | empty | stack + GraceCommandError message | | `… --format json --record false` | 1 | empty | same stack — **no JSON envelope** |
citty `runMain` `process.exit(1)`s on non-CLIError throws after `console.error(error)`. The repository **declares** `GraceCommandErrorEnvelope` (`schemaVersion: "1.0.0"`, `ok: false`, coded `error`) and `runQueryCommand`'s doc promises failures *"without stack traces."* A reachable branch that honours neither is the D13 class: a `schemaVersion`-bearing surface must not answer in a shape its schema does not describe. Latent third part: `runGraceCommand` sets `process.exitCode = commandError.exitCode`; the guard path never reaches that line and takes citty's hard `process.exit(1)`. Both are `1` today (`GraceCommandError` defaults `exitCode` to 1; no production error sets another value), so the divergence is invisible until something needs a different code — nothing pins the contract.
**Two independent instances make this a class, not a one-off.** A repair that fixes the ledger read and leaves the CLI channel (or the reverse) has not addressed the thesis.
**Enabling drift (F24) — not the same defect, required for instance 2.** `M-QUERY` is summarised in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` as *"Artifact query and navigation: module, file, graph, and verification resolution,"* and `src/query/errors.ts` repeats that as file-local `SCOPE`. What it holds is `runGraceCommand`, `GraceCommandError`, the envelope, and (since C-FLAG-HONESTY) `defineGraceCommand` in `src/query/command.ts`. Measured production importers of `query/errors` / `./errors` at authoring HEAD (F12.2; full listing, not truncated): **14 files** —
gates/command.ts, gates/ledger.ts, review/command.ts, grace-cursor.ts, grace-status.ts, grace-lint.ts, grace-context.ts, grace-doctor.ts, grace-module.ts, grace-file.ts, grace-graph.ts, grace-verification.ts, query/core.ts, query/command.ts.
Most of those are not query resolution. Fixing instance 2 *in place* under M-QUERY deepens exactly the drift F24 records. F24 is therefore the **enabling change** for a home that can honestly host the shared error surface — not a third instance of the legibility thesis.

Goals.Goal: Ledger reads expose a discriminated three-exit result for every consumer that currently collapses through `wrapperFromLedger` null: `absent-no-file | unreadable(code, detail) | ok(wrapper)` — not bare null interpreted as "no ledger yet."

`readLatestReviewVerdict`, `listReviewVerdicts`, and `readGateDecisions` (and any successor wrappers) consume that three-exit surface without changing gate permit/refuse outcomes on currently green fixtures (compat). Unreadable never becomes a silent pass at any gate.

Plan-quality and other read-only consumers use the **same** classification surface as gates — no dual parse classification beside a still-collapsing gate path. `readLedgerVerdictsSurface` becomes (or is merged into) the single read, not a second definition that can disagree with `wrapperFromLedger`.

CLI boolean-space refusal (and any other `GraceCommandError` thrown from `defineGraceCommand`'s pre-run path) is rendered through the repository's declared error channel: text mode is a single stderr message without a stack trace; `--format json` yields a parseable `GraceCommandErrorEnvelope` on stdout; exit code comes from `GraceCommandError.exitCode` (pinned exactly, F23), not from citty's hard-coded exit alone.

The space-form refusal continues to prevent the flagged side effect (for `--record false`: no Decision append; no ledger created when none existed). Improving the message while letting the command run fails the goals.
The error-channel repair covers the **class** of live boolean sites under the guard (re-derived via `listBooleanFlags` at implement — **24** at authoring HEAD), not a one-command special case.

Shared CLI infrastructure (`GraceCommandError`, envelope, `runGraceCommand`, `defineGraceCommand`) lives under graph module `M-CLI-INFRA` with matching `V-M-CLI-INFRA`, and the file-local `LINKS` / graph Summary for `src/query/errors.ts` and `src/query/command.ts` describe what those files hold (F24 repair — enabling, disclosed; re-LINKS in place, no directory move).

Constraints.Constraint: Binding: decisions.md F24 (enabling home), F25 (channel hole), D12 (honest new-file/module windows), D13 (schemaVersion surface honesty), F12.2 (measure denominators; do not invent counts), F23 (exact pins, not lower bounds), F10 (tests check what their names claim). Spec only in this authoring pass; status remains `"draft"`; do not author plan.xml until the spec is approved (F4 two-stage).

Additive / fail-closed only for ledger reads. Existing projects without `run-ledger.xml` stay green. Unreadable never becomes a silent pass at any gate. Gate policy is unchanged (D11: apply still requires a recorded verdict when the ledger is readable).

Instance 2 must not weaken C-FLAG-HONESTY: space-form still refuses with both working forms named; bare flag, equals form, and `--no-flag` still work; legitimate positionals still work. The refusal rule is not reopened.

Behaviour, not full mechanism. Feasibility notes: `runGraceCommand` and `GraceCommandErrorEnvelope` already exist; routing the guard through them (or a shared renderer they call) is plan-level. Whether `wrapperFromLedger` is replaced, returns a result type, or is deleted once `readLedgerVerdictsSurface` is the sole classification is plan-level — the binding property is **one** classification definition, not two that can disagree.

AffectedAreas is a closed list and binds the plan (change.plan-scope-exceeds-spec). A plan that needs a module not named here is a stop-and-report. Over-declaring grants unreviewed scope; under-declaring costs a re-spec.

Superseding C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE is the **authority's** act — after this spec is **approved**, **before any plan is authored** for this bundle (`status="superseded"`, a Replacement element naming C-LEGIBLE-FAILURE, move to `archive/`). It cannot happen sooner (`change.superseded-replacement-not-found` requires the replacement to exist); waiting for plan approval would leave two active bundles holding live claims on the same subject. Spec-authoring and plan/execute must not edit, move, or delete that draft. Absorb its substance here.

F24 repair is **re-LINKS in place**, not a physical move. `src/query/errors.ts` and `src/query/command.ts` keep their paths; their `MODULE_CONTRACT` headers change `LINKS: M-QUERY` → `LINKS: M-CLI-INFRA`, and the graph gains an `M-CLI-INFRA` entry true of what those files hold. No import-path rewrites across the fourteen production importers. Directory layout is not the contract surface — this repository already separates directory from module (`src/grace-verification.ts` declares `LINKS: M-LOCALIZE` while that module's graph `Path` is `src/verification/localize.ts`). Consequence: once the two files link elsewhere, `M-QUERY`'s existing Summary becomes true as written with no edit to it.

Accepted residual cost of re-LINKS without move: `src/query/` will hold files belonging to two modules (`M-QUERY` and `M-CLI-INFRA`), so a reader browsing directories rather than contract headers still gets no signal and may imitate by adding the next cross-cutting concern to `query/`. That is a **smaller** harm than F24's original — a header now answers the question correctly — and a physical relocation is a purely mechanical follow-on if it is ever wanted. Legibility is this bundle's subject; layout tidiness is not. A fourteen-file import rewrite on top of the three-exit ledger repair, the channel repair, the exit-code pin, and a new module would make this the largest bundle in the track, which is where quality slips.

`V-M-CLI-INFRA` is **required**, not optional and not "plan-justified alternative home." Lint does not enforce module→verification pairing, but the repository has **19 modules and 19 `V-M-*` anchors, one-to-one**. An invariant like that does not die by being repealed; it dies by acquiring its first exception. A module with no verification anchor is also one that nothing can `MustVerify` against, which would leave this bundle's own assertions pointing at nothing.

Archives under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` and `docs/plans/archive/` are never edited. No CHANGELOG.md edit (D5.5 — new surface text in commit body if any). No package / marketplace / openpackage version surface change unless the plan explicitly requires a graph/verification anchor addition (allowed under AffectedAreas; version bumps still out unless required). No skills/ or plugins/ skill-text change in this bundle.

Evidence doctrine: red-first regressions for each AC. Where a criterion asserts a count (boolean inventory, exit code, Decision append absence), tests pin exact values (F23 — `toBe` / exact absence, not `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`). Re-measure inventory with `listBooleanFlags` (live objects), not a remembered number or source-text grep alone (F10 / F12.2).

NonGoals.NonGoal: Changing gate policy (apply still requires a recorded verdict when readable; approve/archive requirements unchanged).
Changing any flag's default, the boolean space-form refusal *rule*, or citty's equals / `--no-` working forms — C-FLAG-HONESTY is archived and stays.
Migrating off citty, forking citty, or making the equals form (`--flag=false`) an error.
Rewriting `runGraceCommand`'s success path, or inventing a second parallel error envelope schema.
Changing plan-quality's report shape beyond consuming the shared three-exit API (no redesign of plan-quality rows).
skills/ or plugins/ skill-text changes; documentation-only "fix" that leaves either collapse armed.
Other open findings (F9.9 attempt-pair wording, F20 cloneXmlNode home, F21 fix-budget attempts vs failures, F22 paused-pending-approval self-clear) — each has or will have its own bundle.
Choosing `M-CLI` as the infrastructure home — that anchor is `src/grace.ts` (dispatch root), not shared CLI infrastructure.

Physical relocation of `src/query/errors.ts` / `src/query/command.ts` (or any of their fourteen production importers' import paths). F24 is repaired by graph entry + re-LINKS; a move is a mechanical follow-on if ever wanted, not this bundle's subject.
Widening M-QUERY's Summary/SCOPE to absorb CLI infrastructure instead of introducing `M-CLI-INFRA` — rejected so the name keeps predicting contents.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-THREE-EXITS: Ledger read distinguishes `absent-no-file`, `unreadable` (with stable `code` and `detail`), and `ok` (wrapper available / section walkable). **Discriminating negatives:** a truncated or non-parseable file is **unreadable, not absent**; a missing file is **absent, not unreadable**; a parseable ledger with no wrapper for the change id is **unreadable** with code `ledger.bundle-id-mismatch` (already used by `readLedgerVerdictsSurface` — must not remain collapsed to absent via `wrapperFromLedger` null). **Failure conditions:** bare null still returned to gate consumers; two competing classifications that can disagree for the same path; unreadable reported as absent.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-GATE-COMPAT: Gate apply / approve / archive outcomes on the existing suite fixtures are unchanged. Fail-closed refuse on corrupt or invalid ledger content remains refuse (not throw-out-of-band, not permit). **Discriminating negative:** a deliberate regression that turns a fail-closed refuse into throw-or-permit fails a test. **Failure conditions:** green fixture suite flips permit ↔ refuse; unreadable becomes silent pass.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SINGLE-CLASSIFICATION: Plan-quality (`collectPlanQualityReport` / `readLedgerVerdictsSurface` consumers) and gate decision paths share **one** ledger-parse classification definition. No private re-implementation of absent/unreadable/ok beside a collapsing `wrapperFromLedger`. **Discriminating negative:** removing or breaking the shared surface makes plan-quality **and** gate ledger tests red, not only one side. **Failure conditions:** dual APIs that can classify the same file differently; plan-quality still special-casing while gates keep null collapse.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHANNEL-JSON-ENVELOPE: For any boolean space-form refusal under a command that declares `--format` (or otherwise supports JSON error mode), invoking with `--format json` and the space form exits non-zero and writes a **valid** `GraceCommandErrorEnvelope` to stdout (`schemaVersion: "1.0.0"`, `ok: false`, `error.code`, `error.message`) — assert by `JSON.parse` of entire stdout, not substring. No stack frame on stdout. **Failure conditions:** empty stdout; unparseable stdout; envelope missing required fields; stack-only stderr with empty stdout counted as success.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHANNEL-TEXT-LEGIBLE: In text mode, the same refusal exits non-zero with a single stderr message (no stack trace) that still names both working forms for the flag involved (equals and `--no-`/bare), matching C-FLAG-HONESTY information content. **Failure conditions:** stack dump as the primary user-visible form; message that omits working forms; exit 0.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHANNEL-SIDE-EFFECT-HELD: Space-form refusal still prevents the flagged side effect. For the F18 incident shape on a **temp fixture only**: `ngrace gate apply|archive|approve --change C-* --record false` creates no new Decision and does not create a ledger when none existed (exact Decision count `toBe` before/after — F23). **Failure conditions:** Decision append; ledger created; infer-and- continue; rewrite-argv-and-continue.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXIT-CODE-FROM-ERROR: Process exit status for a rendered `GraceCommandError` equals `error.exitCode` from the thrown object (default 1 today), not an unrelated hard-coded path that merely coincides. **Pin exactly (F23).** **Discriminating proof:** a test (or fixture) that constructs a `GraceCommandError` with a non-default `exitCode` (e.g. 2) and drives it through the same render path used by the guard must observe that exit code. **Failure conditions:** exit always 1 regardless of `error.exitCode`; only "non-zero" asserted.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CHANNEL-CLASS-COVERAGE: The error-channel repair applies to the class of live boolean sites under `defineGraceCommand` (re-measure with `listBooleanFlags` at close — **24** at authoring HEAD). Not a one-leaf special case for gate `--record`. **Failure conditions:** only gate leaves render the envelope; a live branded site still hits citty's stack path for space-form.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INFRA-HOME-TRUE: After the change, `src/query/errors.ts` and `src/query/command.ts` declare `LINKS: M-CLI-INFRA`, and `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` has an `M-CLI-INFRA` entry whose Summary describes shared CLI infrastructure (`GraceCommandError`, envelope, `runGraceCommand`, `defineGraceCommand`) — **true of what those files hold**. Matching `V-M-CLI-INFRA` exists (one-to-one with modules). Directory placement is **not** a criterion: re-LINKS in place satisfies this AC; a physical move is neither required nor in scope. **Failure conditions:** either file still `LINKS: M-QUERY` while holding CLI infra; `M-CLI-INFRA` graph entry missing or with a false Summary/SCOPE (D12 class); `V-M-CLI-INFRA` missing; criterion treated as requiring a directory move or import-path rewrite.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-AND-LINT: Red-first regressions cover each AC above with exact assertions where a number or presence/absence is claimed (F23). `bun test` for touched packages green; `bun run validate:ci` green; `bun run ngrace lint --path .` is 0 errors and 0 warnings at close; `ngrace review --path .` is 0 findings on a clean tree after the change. No edits under `docs/plans/archive/` or `.ngrace/changes/archive/`; no CHANGELOG.md; no version / marketplace / openpackage version surface unless required for a new graph/V-M-* anchor declared in the plan; no skills/ or plugins/ skill-text edits. **Failure conditions:** suite red; lint or review dirty by design silence; archive edits; dual active specs both claiming the ledger repair after authority supersession is complete.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Red-first: three-exit matrix (absent / unreadable / ok) with discriminating negatives (truncated ≠ absent; missing ≠ unreadable; wrong wrapper id → ledger.bundle-id-mismatch); gate outcomes unchanged on green fixtures and still fail-closed on corrupt ledger; plan-quality and gates share one classification; space-form --record false still writes no Decision (exact count); --format json space-form parses as GraceCommandErrorEnvelope; text mode no stack, names working forms; exitCode from error object pinned with a non-default exitCode probe; listBooleanFlags count exact at close (24 at authoring) and channel covers branded sites; errors.ts and command.ts LINKS M-CLI-INFRA; graph M-CLI-INFRA Summary true of what they hold; V-M-CLI-INFRA present (19↔19 preserved). Dogfood: ngrace lint --path . 0/0; ngrace review --path . 0 findings; validate:ci green.

Assumptions.Assumption: F24 decision **chosen: new module `M-CLI-INFRA`** — id fixed, not provisional; does not collide with `M-CLI` (`src/grace.ts`, dispatch root). Cost: graph anchor + **required** `V-M-CLI-INFRA` (19 modules / 19 `V-M-*` one-to-one; no first exception), and re-LINKS of `src/query/errors.ts` and `src/query/command.ts` to `M-CLI-INFRA` (no directory move; no import-path rewrites). Rejected alternative: widen M-QUERY Summary/SCOPE only — cheaper and immediately true, but the name stops predicting contents and future cross-cutting CLI concerns still land by imitation. Rejected alternative: physical move of the two files plus fourteen importer rewrites — layout tidiness, not legibility, and bundle-size risk. Not M-CLI.

Lint window for a not-yet-created module id in AffectedAreas: at **spec draft alone**, lint does not require graph membership of AffectedAreas tags (coverage is plan DurableScope vs spec; AffectedAreas tags are not graph-resolved at spec stage). Measured expectation while this draft has no plan.xml: **0 errors from the invented anchor alone**. When a plan is authored, DurableScope GraphAnchors must name M-CLI-INFRA and the graph entry must exist before LINKS resolve — that is a **plan/execute** window, not a silent falsification of SCOPE. D12 authorized the analogous window for a **not-yet-created file** on OWS (change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope until the file exists with true LINKS). Same reasoning holds for a **not-yet-created module** between plan authoring and the task that writes the graph entry + re-LINKS on the two files: predicted, short-lived, must be 0/0 at close. If execute discovers the window is unworkable (e.g. lint errors on unknown GraphAnchors before the graph file is written in the same task), stop-and-report rather than falsify contracts.

Module ids in AffectedAreas, measured against graph and file-local LINKS at authoring (closed list of four): **M-CLI-INFRA** — new host: `src/query/errors.ts`, `src/query/command.ts` (re-LINKS; does not exist yet); **M-QUERY** — loses those two files' LINKS (Summary stays true as written; Path remains `src/query/core.ts`); **M-GATES** — `gates/ledger.ts` three exits, and the gate consumers (`readLatestReviewVerdict`, `readGateDecisions`, gate command path); **M-REVIEW** — `listReviewVerdicts`, and `review/outcomes.ts` plan-quality sharing the classification. Seven former candidates dropped: channel repair lives entirely inside `defineGraceCommand` (`src/query/command.ts`), so no CLI entry point is edited; `src/grace-doctor.ts` only consumes `collectPlanQualityReport`, whose report shape is a NonGoal. If a plan later cannot proceed without a dropped module, that is a stop-and-report and a re-spec.

`readLedgerVerdictsSurface` already implements the three-way distinction for Verdicts (corr 185 / C-REPORT-HONESTY) without changing gate behaviour. The work is making that classification **the** read for gate decision paths too (or a shared primitive both call), not inventing a third API. Wrong-wrapper already codes `ledger.bundle-id-mismatch` on the surface path; wrapperFromLedger still returns null for that case.
Live boolean sites via listBooleanFlags at authoring HEAD: **24** (factory expansion of gate --record ×3 + 21 other live sites). Channel coverage is over that live set.

C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE remains draft under active/ and byte-identical until the authority supersedes it **after this spec is approved and before any plan for this bundle is authored**. This bundle claims its substance; dual concurrent active bundles holding live claims on the same subject must not persist past approval (and dual concurrent plans on the same OWS must not execute in parallel — F10.2 style sequencing). Spec authoring does not touch that directory.

File layout under `src/query/` is **decided**: errors.ts and command.ts stay where they are; only LINKS (and their file-local SCOPE/PURPOSE if currently false) and the new graph/`V-M-CLI-INFRA` entries change. Whether `defineGraceCommand` routes through `runGraceCommand` by shared renderer or by wrapping is plan-level mechanism. Binding: contracts true of the files as written; channel criteria above; no import-path rewrites.
